The must-sees

8 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church · 1913

    Blue Church

    Ödön Lechner designed the Church of St Elizabeth, and it was completed in 1913. Even its roof tiles are blue-glazed.

    Look for

    Above the entrance, a mosaic shows St Elizabeth of Hungary with roses in her lap.

  2. 02
    Fortress

    Bratislava Castle

    It burned in 1811 and stood as a ruin until it was rebuilt from the 1950s on. Today it holds exhibitions of the Slovak National Museum and is used for state occasions.

    Look for

    From the terraces you can see across the Danube into Austria, and on a clear day toward Hungary.

  3. 03
    Fortress

    Devín Castle

    The rock was a stronghold in the time of Great Moravia, and the castle was blown up by Napoleon’s troops in 1809. Under communism the border here was part of the Iron Curtain, and a memorial nearby remembers people killed trying to cross it.

    Look for

    Below the castle, a tiny tower perches on a rock above the river. Legend tells of a young woman who leapt from it for love.

  4. 04
    Square

    Main Square

    Markets have been held here since the Middle Ages, and today the Christmas market fills it in December. The French embassy occupies one of the palaces on the north side.

    Look for

    On top of the fountain stands a knight in armour. The story goes that once a year, on New Year’s Eve, he turns around.

  5. 05
    Fortress

    Michael’s Gate

    The gate dates from the 14th century, and its baroque top was added in the 1750s. Inside the tower is a museum of arms and the old fortifications.

    Look for

    In the passage under the gate, a plaque in the pavement marks kilometre zero, with distances to cities around the world.

  6. 06
    Bridge · 1972

    Most SNP (UFO Bridge)

    It opened in 1972, named after the Slovak National Uprising of 1944. Building its approach road meant demolishing much of the old Jewish quarter below the castle, including the Neolog synagogue.

    Look for

    One leg of the pylon hides a lift that carries visitors up to the saucer.

  7. 07
    Palace · 1781

    Primate’s Palace

    Built in 1781 for the Archbishop of Esztergom, it is now the seat of the city mayor. The Peace of Pressburg between France and Austria was signed in its Hall of Mirrors in 1805, after the Battle of Austerlitz.

    Look for

    In the courtyard, a fountain shows St George fighting the dragon.

  8. 08
    Church

    St. Martin’s Cathedral

    Between 1563 and 1830 eleven Hungarian kings and eight royal consorts were crowned here, Maria Theresa among them. The crown on the spire is a gilded copy of the Hungarian royal crown.

    Look for

    Inside, Georg Raphael Donner’s statue shows St Martin on horseback, dressed as a Hungarian hussar, cutting his cloak for a beggar.
